markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Users distinguish specific interests from broad relevance. Recent pooling may emphasize current interests, but cannot supply missing semantic distinctions. (2) Incidental purchases can imply unsupported equipment or project needs. Decay can attenuate older incidental evidence, while amplifying recent accidents. (3) Electronics has training-margin p10=0.3256 and 7.67% negative margins. These motivate discrimination experiments without establishing validation benefit or harmful embedding collapse.

**Literature insights.** (1) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) motivates objective-first comparisons; it does not establish CE superiority here. (2) [MARS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) motivates separating interests, although its pretrained-content assumptions differ. (3) [TALE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.07382) supports simple temporal baselines; recency does not identify compatibility or satisfied needs. (4) [DIN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978) supplies a direct candidate-conditioning precedent, making that extension less original than previously implied.

Three directions follow: improve candidate discrimination, isolate temporal evidence from added capacity, and require evidence before adding candidate-dependent matching.

### Framework

| Representation / objective | Baseline objective | Uniform multi-negative CE |
|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Reference | A: objective isolation |
| Bounded recency residual | Optional interaction control | B: simple context adaptation |
| Bounded candidate-conditioned residual | Deferred | C: selective interest matching |

### Ideas and assessments

Scores are prospective; difficulty 10 means hardest. Each cell gives **score: positive / negative**.

| Dimension | A: CE only | B: recency + CE | C: candidate conditioning + CE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Originality | 2: clean isolation / established | 3: bounded integration / familiar pooling | 4: selective residual / DIN precedent |
| Future potential | 6: reusable foundation / limited representation | 6: extensible baseline / decay oversimplifies intent | 7: preserves interests / costly exhaustive scoring |
| User alignment | 3: discrimination / no context mechanism | 5: current evidence and attenuated old accidents / recent accidents remain | 6: candidate-specific evidence / can reinforce substitutes |
| Model alignment | 7: targets weak margins / scale can mislead | 6: contextual separation / no assured improvement | 6: conditional separation / additional overfitting |
| Difficulty | 3: unchanged inference / sampler changes | 5: simple recurrence / controlled comparisons and export parity | 7: familiar attention / full-catalog cost and diagnostic adaptation |

### Selected idea: bounded recency residual with CE

At 20% progress, retain **B**, staged after A. It targets **broad thematic matches** through recent context and **unsupported specialized recommendations** through attenuation of older incidental evidence. These are explicit, limited hypotheses: it cannot infer ownership, compatibility, unmet need, or fine content distinctions. CE targets Electronics’ weak lower-tail training separation. Existing evidence does not justify a new, more expensive model.

Use normalized exponential pooling: `S=q*S+m*e; Z=q*Z+m; p=S/max(Z,eps)`, with `q=exp(-beta)`. Accumulate in float32, preserve autograd, and mask padding outputs. Project `p`, cap its norm at `0.25*||h||`, and add it through a zero-initialized tanh gate. Train CE with 32 uniform training-complement negatives. Zero gating recovers baseline features initially only when backbone initialization matches; subsequent backbone updates and bounded corrections can change rankings.

Compare baseline → A → B using identical shared initialization, batches, negatives, and checkpoint rules. Optional controls are uniform pooling, fixed decay, last-item pooling, projection controls, repetition weighting, and auxiliary-branch shuffling; predeclare a budget-limited subset. Learnable decay may exploit popular recent items or repetition rather than intent. Report decay half-life, frequency-stratified sensitivity, runtime, and fixed-example margins without treating them as selection objectives.

Preserve all four routes, seeds, diagnostic interfaces, and predictor parity. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10. Bootstrap paired hits within category only if exposed by the unchanged evaluator; winner intervals remain exploratory after adaptive selection. Predeclare comparisons, stopping, and tie-breaking. Charge search execution against 43,200 summed GPU-seconds, reserving validation, diagnostics, failures, and simulator scoring; record final held-out inference separately. Historical 0.5762 lacks a controlled comparison and establishes no benefit for B.

idea.description: First isolate uniform multi-negative candidate-set cross-entropy, then test a bounded, candidate-independent recency residual around causal SASRec. Retain this inexpensive hypothesis at 20% research progress, with explicit controls for recency, added capacity, repeated items, and validation selection. Defer candidate-conditioned attention until a separately budgeted comparison is warranted.
idea.motivation: The representation targets two observed user-facing failures: broad thematic matches crowding out specific current interests, and specialized recommendations supported mainly by incidental historical purchases. Its proposed mechanisms are emphasis on recent behavioral context and attenuation of older incidental evidence. These mechanisms may fail when recent purchases are accidental, when persistent interests are old, or when recommendations require unavailable compatibility or unmet-need information. Multi-negative CE separately targets the model-facing weakness of lower-tail training separation, especially in Electronics. Neither training margins nor embedding alignment establishes generalization, recommendation diversity, or user usefulness.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an experimental specification, not implemented or validated evidence. Retain RecHarness sasrec_perdataset preprocessing, splits, mappings, backbone, optimizer, batching, training targets, validation cadence, and checkpoint rules unless explicitly ablated. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')). Retain every dataset route and write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Record the resolved baseline hyperparameters, validation schedule, checkpoint-selection rule, library versions, sampler settings, and architecture configuration in trial artifacts; do not invent unspecified baseline values.

Define recency by sequence position, not timestamps. Let beta=softplus(beta_raw), initialized to 0.1 using beta_raw=log(expm1(0.1)), and q=exp(-beta). For raw item embedding e_t and valid-token mask m_t, initialize S=0 and Z=0, then compute S_t=q*S_(t-1)+m_t*e_t and Z_t=q*Z_(t-1)+m_t. Return p_t=S_t/clamp_min(Z_t,1e-8), and zero all padding outputs. This is an adjusted exponentially weighted mean. Padding consumes a sequence position under this declared recurrence; left padding contributes no history. Do not silently change internal-padding semantics between training and inference. Accumulate S and Z in float32 with out-of-place operations, avoid inverse powers of q, and retain beta's autograd connection. Work is O(Ld), streaming state is O(d), and training autograd retains intermediate states. Report beta and positional half-life log(2)/beta. Exact uniform pooling is a separate beta=0 mode, since finite softplus parameters cannot produce exact zero.

Use a bias-free d-by-d projection W with a declared Xavier-uniform initialization. Form r=W*p and r_bounded=r*min(1,0.25*norm(h)/clamp_min(norm(r),1e-8)). Compute features=h+tanh(g)*r_bounded, with one scalar g per dataset initialized exactly to zero. The cap is a fixed experimental choice rather than an established optimum. Norms are computed along the feature dimension. Empty histories return zero branch outputs. At initialization, identical backbone parameters and zero gating recover baseline features; branch parameters initially receive zero gradient until the gate moves. Subsequent shared-backbone updates can change baseline scores, and the cap does not guarantee unchanged rankings or HR@10. Use precisely the same feature path in training, validation, diagnostics, and prediction.

Sample K=32 independent uniform negatives with replacement from the nonpadding catalog excluding each user's complete observed training history, including the positive target. Keep user identity privately available to the sampler; do not reconstruct exclusions from truncated sequences. Preserve duplicate negative draws. Skip and count supervised examples with empty complements. Never consult validation or test interactions for exclusions. Unknown positives remain possible false negatives. Use temperature-1 CE over [positive, 32 negatives], target column zero, without logQ correction. This defines a candidate-set objective, not an unbiased full-catalog likelihood. If memory requires chunking, normalize summed losses by the total valid-position count and use supported activation checkpointing or an equivalent memory-safe backward strategy; ordinary summation of chunk losses retains their graphs. Record execution cost. Retain the baseline objective unchanged in the reference run.

Predeclare baseline, CE-only, and learned-recency-plus-CE comparisons before inspecting their outcomes. Where the budget permits, add recency with the baseline objective to isolate objective–representation interaction. Use identical shared-parameter initialization, training examples, ordering, and relevant negatives across controlled comparisons. Use separate deterministic RNG streams for auxiliary initialization, training sampling, and diagnostics; adding a projection must not shift backbone initialization or sampled negatives. Record stream seeds and deterministic settings. One training seed satisfies this protocol but cannot establish robustness across initialization or training order.

Optional controls must be selected and budgeted in advance rather than expanded adaptively: exact uniform pooling, fixed beta=0.1, learned decay, and last-valid-item pooling with identical projection and fusion modules; identity/no-projection controls to inspect capacity effects; ordinary occurrence weighting versus causal per-prefix unique-item or inverse-count pooling; and deterministic shuffling confined to the auxiliary branch, preserving counts while disrupting recency. These interventions leave input histories and backbone inputs unchanged. Do not change target or recency sampling while attributing effects to representation. Shuffling can introduce distribution shift and does not establish causality. A complete factorial study is not required within the budget. gBCE is a legitimate alternative objective motivated by gSASRec, but is deferred rather than claimed inferior.

Track learned gate, beta, half-life, residual norms, per-category and macro validation HR@10, and actual GPU time. Use fixed diagnostic examples and negatives across variants. Raw-margin improvements can arise from changed logit scale, so optionally report normalized-score sensitivity with its definition alongside the original raw-logit metrics. Higher mean embedding cosine alone does not establish harmful collapse or diversity. Centered covariance effective rank and training-frequency-stratified summaries may provide additional descriptive checks if budgeted; they are not selection objectives. Recency and repeated-item pooling may encode popularity, redundancy, or short-term accidents rather than specific intent. Report qualitative user-failure changes only when simulator feedback is actually supplied, without inventing rejection labels or semantic metadata.

Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve diagnostic batches (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors B x L. view.model must reference the actual trained module; view.item_emb remains accessible, and view.log2feats plus view.predict_score must include the complete selected scoring path. Use evaluation mode and restore the prior training state afterward. Record unavailable metadata explicitly. Only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions are available; the generic metadata examples do not authorize review content, ratings, prices, stores, item categories, simulator traits, external data, or pretrained weights.

Serialize the architecture mode, projection, gate, decay parameters, dimensions, mappings, configuration, and checkpoint beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the exact trained module and routes all four datasets correctly. Disable dropout during scoring. Retain the established seen-item exclusion and ranking/tie rules. Candidate-independent recency pooling encodes each history once and preserves dot-product candidate scoring. Benchmark full-catalog unseen-item scoring, including exclusion and top-k overhead, for the prescribed 20 real training users, five per category; sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog usefulness.

Candidate-conditioned pooling remains a subsequent declared experiment. DIN supplies a direct precedent; a normalized softmax attention variant is an adaptation rather than the original unnormalized activation formula. It would require causal history states, padding masks, zero output for empty histories, candidate chunking, exact exhaustive top-k merging, and adapted scoring diagnostics. Dot-product candidate attention adds O(NLd) work; chunking reduces memory rather than total work. Cache history projections and normalize over history separately for each candidate. Do not adopt it merely because it is more expressive.

Select only using the unchanged pinned evaluator's four-category macro validation HR@10, with the prescribed 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42. Preserve baseline validation cadence and checkpoint rules consistently; record the maximum comparison count and stopping policy before running, and resolve exact ties by lower measured inference cost, then earlier checkpoint. If paired per-user hit indicators are exposed without evaluator changes, compute the observed macro difference and a 95% paired bootstrap interval from 10,000 resamples using a recorded fixed seed, independently resampling users within each category while sharing sampled indices across models. These intervals condition on the trained models and pinned candidates and omit training-seed and candidate-generation variation. Winner intervals after adaptive checkpoint/configuration selection are exploratory. Simultaneous bounds for a fixed declared family can address multiplicity but cannot remove unrecorded adaptive-search bias. If paired outputs are unavailable, report that limitation rather than reconstructing or inventing them.

Before execution, record a practical gain threshold and simulator inference latency/memory ceilings appropriate to the host; numerical values are not supplied here and must not be represented as established requirements. Prefer simpler models when evidence is inconclusive. Reserve projected training, validation, diagnostics, debugging, simulator scoring, and failure costs before each trial. Keep every run single-GPU; concurrent trials consume summed GPU time against 43,200 GPU-seconds. Record LLM time and final held-out inference separately as prescribed. Never inspect hidden test files or modify the evaluator. The historical 0.5762 is not a controlled comparison demonstrating this proposal's benefit.
idea.pseudocode:
Declare variants = [baseline, CE_only, learned_recency_CE]
Record resolved baseline config, validation/checkpoint rules, comparison limit, stopping and tie-breaking
Preserve preprocessing_seed=0, training_seed=42, four dataset mappings and routes
Read DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
Read epochs = int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200'))
Use deterministic separate RNG streams; match shared initialization and batch/negative streams
Reserve summed GPU execution budget before each trial

For each variant and training batch:
    h = SASRec(sequence)  # causal features for predicting next items
    if variant == learned_recency_CE:
        beta = softplus(beta_raw)  # initialize beta=0.1
        q = exp(-beta)
        S, Z = float32_zeros(), float32_zeros()
        pooled = []
        for t in sequence positions:
            m = (sequence[:, t] != 0)
            e = float32(item_emb(sequence[:, t]))
            S = q*S + m[:, None]*e
            Z = q*Z + m
            p = S / clamp_min(Z[:, None], 1e-8)
            pooled.append(where(m[:, None], p, 0))
        r = bias_free_projection(stack(pooled))
        r = r * min(1, 0.25*norm(h)/clamp_min(norm(r), 1e-8))
        h = h + tanh(g)*r  # scalar gate initialized to zero
    if variant == baseline:
        loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(h)
    else:
        negatives, eligible = uniform_training_complement_samples(
            privately_available_user_ids, K=32, replacement=True)
        count skipped empty-complement examples
        valid = eligible AND positive_is_nonpadding
        if no valid positions: continue
        loss = sum_CE_over_valid_positions(h, positive, negatives, temperature=1) / count(valid)
        # positive column=0; no logQ correction; checkpoint chunks if needed
    backward(loss)
    optimizer.step()

Run unchanged pinned validation schedule and record every comparison
Select exclusively by four-category macro HR@10 using declared rules
Report category deltas, GPU cost, gate, beta, half-life, and fixed-example diagnostics
If unchanged evaluator exposes paired hits:
    paired_bootstrap_within_each_category(replicates=10000, fixed_recorded_seed)
    label post-selection intervals exploratory
Run DiagnosisProbe through exact selected feature/scoring paths
Export checkpoint, architecture configuration, mappings, and matching predictor writer
Measure prescribed full-catalog simulator scoring cost within search budget
Consider candidate conditioning only as a separately declared and budgeted trial

originality.positive: Combines bounded context adaptation with explicit objective-first and capacity-controlled experiments tied to the supplied diagnoses.
originality.negative: Exponential means, residual gates, SASRec, and multi-negative CE are established; DIN also supplies a direct precedent for the deferred candidate-conditioned extension.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive, interpretable reference for later temporal and multi-interest models while separating objective and representation effects.
future_potential.negative: One positional decay curve cannot identify unmet need, compatibility, or fine semantic preference, and may amplify recent accidents or popularity shortcuts.

code_difficulty.positive: The masked recurrence is linear in history length, retains candidate-independent features, and supports standard dot-product inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Matched RNG streams, complete-history sampling exclusions, autograd-safe pooling, memory-safe loss computation, diagnostic compatibility, controlled comparisons, and predictor parity require substantial care.

related_work.title: gSASRec (2024 extended abstract)
contributions: Motivates revisiting sampled BCE overconfidence and testing more negatives and generalized BCE.
Supports isolating objective changes before attributing improvements to history representations.
limitations: Does not establish candidate-set CE superiority over gBCE on the pinned benchmark.
Does not directly resolve unnecessary recommendations, ownership, or compatibility.

related_work.title: MARS (CIKM 2024)
contributions: Uses multiple attribute-aware user and item representations to capture preferences obscured by a single summary.
Motivates later experiments separating interests and candidate-dependent matching.
limitations: Its pretrained-language-model assumptions differ from the prohibition on pretrained weights.
Does not validate the proposed recency residual on these four categories.

related_work.title: TALE (WSDM 2025)
contributions: Studies interval-aware linear item-item prediction and changing-popularity normalization.
Supports considering simple temporal baselines before complex recurrence models.
limitations: Its time-aware mechanism differs from positional exponential pooling.
Temporal evidence alone does not identify satisfied needs, duplication, or compatibility.

related_work.title: pandas exponentially weighted window documentation
contributions: Provides a mathematical reference for the proposed numerator/denominator recurrence.
limitations: Documentation does not establish recommendation effectiveness.
PyTorch masking, initialization, and autograd behavior require explicit implementation.

related_work.title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
contributions: Introduces candidate-specific activation of historical behaviors.
Supplies a direct architectural precedent for deferred candidate-conditioned pooling.
limitations: Normalized softmax attention is an adaptation rather than the original DIN weighting formula.
Candidate-dependent aggregation increases exhaustive full-catalog scoring cost.

related_work.title: SASRec: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequential backbone retained by the proposal.
Grounds the requirement that prefix features exclude future interactions.
limitations: Does not establish the efficacy of the added residual or candidate-set objective.
The pinned RecHarness implementation remains authoritative for baseline details.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides precedent for paired bootstrap comparisons.
Motivates preserving paired observations when estimating model differences.
limitations: Category-stratified recommendation resampling is an adaptation.
Ordinary bootstrap intervals do not account for adaptive validation selection or training-seed variability.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains limitations of recommendation metrics computed with sampled candidates.
Supports restricting conclusions to the prescribed candidate protocol.
limitations: Does not invalidate the benchmark's prescribed selection metric.
Does not provide full-catalog utility evidence for the proposed model.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains optimism introduced by repeated model selection.
Supports prespecified comparison limits and independent final assessment.
limitations: Prespecification and multiplicity handling cannot eliminate undocumented adaptive-search bias.
Does not supply a benchmark-specific practical improvement threshold.
